see.b: Kind of an adventure-tourism park with Nile crocodile feedings, tortoise holding, ostrich viewing, horse/dromedary rides, and boat rides. One croc feeding takes place on Sundays at 16:30. Also a restaurant on site.

see.b: Where visitors can learn about Nairobi, its history and culture. The museum was founded in 1910.

This is a museum housing only special exhibits, so the featured artwork is always changing.

Of interest if you have read Karen Blixen’s book Out of Africa or the movie. Her house is now the home of the museum. You have to be accompanied by a guide to visit the house, but you can walk around the gardens on your own. If you're…
Portrays Kenya’s culture. Visitors can see exhibits of traditional Kenyan homes, artifacts, dances, music, and song.

This is home to large herds of zebra, wildebeest, buffalo, giraffe, lion, cheetah, hippo, and birdlife (over 400 species). Here you can also go on the Nairobi Safari Walk, an educational centre to make people aware of wildlife and…

They take in orphaned elephants from all over Kenya, and keep them until they are able to survive in the wild. Visiting hours are daily at 11:00, so you should aim to arrive about 10 minutes before that time. You will be admitted and…

Spacious park in the city centre. Attractions include a monument, playground, boat rental.

Built in remembrance of the struggle for independence, which Kenya was granted in 1963. The monument is a 24-m (79 ft) high triumphal column supporting a pair of clasped hands and the dove of peace, high over a statue of freedom fighter…
Very nice park to walk and to relax from the hectic town. Because of entrance fee you will not be molested by beggars, sellers, etc.

has an area of 1 063 ha, making it largest of three main gazetted forests in Nairobi (the others are Ngong Forest and Ololua Forest). One of the best forest parks to walk, run, ride, picnic relatively close to the city. It is safe, well…

The city park is a good place to spend leisure time without any disturbance within an indigenous forest and with lots of sykes monkeys. They are trustful and come close due to being fed by visitors frequently. As they expect food from…

Cathedral of the Anglican Church of Kenya, built in 1924.

see.n: Cathedral Basilica of the Holy Family
see.b: Striking modernist Catholic Church Cathedral designed in 1960. The Basilica is the seat of the Archdiocese of Nairobi.
Built in a Victorian architecture style in 1922 by the Isma'ilism community led by Aga Khan.
The only functioning synagogue in East Africa.

Centred on a 2,146m (7,141 ft) mountain, this is mountain forests and plains, with a large population of Buffalo. It also serves as a refuge for Colobus monkeys, bushbuck, duiker, leopard, and a large variety of bird species. Another…

A beautiful tea farm, about 40 minutes away from the city centre of Nairobi. The farm house is set within beautiful gardens surrounded by acres of tea and indigenous forest - home to the colobus monkey and plenty of other wildlife.

In this imaginative place, beautiful art objects are made of recycled glass and exhibited in a lovely garden, In a shop different types of glassware are on sale. Guided presentations take place every 30 min.

Salt lake with hot springs for SPA, soda ash and salt production and many flamingos

A former warehouse turned arts centre - this has also happened in Nairobi and this spot allows you to get a glimpse of what contemporary Kenyan artists are up to, including exhibitions, performances and discussions.

Visit Village Market and Sherlocks.
Nairobi has a great variety of international food. For more information see the Eat section.
Go dancing and be a part of Nairobi's excellent nightlife. For more information see the Drink-section.

Lend a hand at the volunteer-operated school, take a tour of Kibera, and have a cup of tea with the OCC Founder. The founder of the school lives in Kibera and works to provide children in need with education and meals.
Go ice-skating at Panari.

eat.b: A chain restaurant serving local food. Several venues in Nairobi CBD. Spacious with ample seating, reasonably clean.

In the city centre facing the matatu station on Tom Mboya Rd. Regular local prices with more selection, excellent food, friendly service. Very busy at lunchtime.
Near Yaya centre- great Ethiopian food for around USD5-6, although they serve Nescafé coffee rather than the traditional Ethiopian freshly-roasted beans.

An authentic Eritrean restaurant located on the top floor of China Centre on Ngong Road near the Chinese embassy. Meals cost around Ksh 500 and the food is excellent, with nice traditional coffee ceremony.

eat.a: Muguga Green, Off Brookside Grove, Off Waiyaki Way
eat.b: An Ethiopian restaurant with delicious food.

An authentic Ethiopian restaurant with great and affordable food (typical of Ethiopian restaurants in Nairobi!)

Has an array of different ethnic cuisines, including Thai, Italian, Chinese and German, as well as a Mongolian Barbecue. Good prices as well. Venture further into Village Market to find a good Japanese restaurant as well, though with…

Located in Westlands, has fantastic Japanese food. For a price.
Past Village Market and into Runda, is said to have very good food, and is popular with the expat crowd.
On State House Hill at the Palacina Hotel, a very upmarket bistro fusion grill restaurant in a lovely outdoor setting. Fantastic food.

Many Kenyan dishes, but also many dishes from other African countries
Amazing seafood and spectacular decor a must visit.
The New Florida, locally known as Madhouse or Madi, is in the heart of Nairobi on Koinange Street.
Commerce House, 1st Floor. The latest addition to the Florida Group.
Handpicked music by the DJ. The bar offers a varied food menu along with a long list of signature cocktails, fine wines and liquors.

eat.pr: Shooters and cocktails range US$3-6 with shooters and high end, globally popular

Live music, cocktails.
Great place to watch Formula 1.
Many expats and travellers and has a cover band that plays very good music. A lot of ladies of the night here, always after the expats.

Located downtown and a branch in Parklands, next to the local Police Station.
